title: channel_claims table — exactly-once handoff claim (INSERT-to-claim, 409 already_claimed)

epic.name: Coordination Bus v2 (re-scoped): Repo Coordination Bus

story.as_a: one of several concurrent agents that could pick up the same handoff
story.i_want_to: claim a handoff exactly once so exactly one agent owns it, losers get a clean 409, and done-state is explicit
story.so_that: beelink->mac-mini #812 is 'handled exactly once, not dropped and not double-done' — the value the v1 bus never delivered

rationale: The panel's critical shipped blocker: loopctl is agent-native, multi-tenant, and CONCURRENT — two mac-mini sessions can both act on #812, or none do. There is no claim primitive. And it CANNOT be bolted onto the existing keyed post: the shipped slot key includes the server-stamped `agent_id` (channel_posts_session_key_uidx, hardened at 20260718000000:22-25) and session_id, and insert_opts/1 routes ANY keyed post into an owner-scoped upsert (coordination.ex:355-365) — so a different agent writing the 'same' claim key just makes a NEW slot, never a claim. A claim is structurally impossible on that surface. It needs a dedicated table whose uniqueness is on `(tenant_id, project_id, ref)` — NOT on the claimant — so the FIRST inserter wins and everyone else conflicts. The panel proved the concurrency: INSERT-to-claim with a UNIQUE constraint is atomic at the DB; the loser's INSERT violates the constraint and maps to 409, with no read-then-write TOCTOU window.

background.reference: panel agreed-gap #2 ('No claim / ack-once + no done-state') and the 'Open tension' resolution (the architect's thin 'claim via keyed upsert' collides with the owner-scoped slot key — so a dedicated table is the only correct path); insert_opts/1 (coordination.ex:355-365); the hardened slot index (20260718000000:22-25).
background.includes: A new channel_claims table + Loopctl.Coordination claim/release/done functions + MCP tools, following the AdminRepo + explicit-tenant-filter + audit-in-Multi conventions of the existing coordination context.

acceptance_criteria.description: New `channel_claims` table: `id` (binary_id pk), `tenant_id` (FK, NOT NULL), `project_id` (FK, NOT NULL), `ref text NOT NULL` (the claimed anchor, e.g. "handoff:repo#812"), `claimant_agent_id` (FK to agents, NOT NULL, server-stamped), `claimed_at` (NOT NULL), `done_at` (NULL until done), `lease_expires_at` (NOT NULL), timestamps. A UNIQUE index on `(tenant_id, project_id, ref)` is the exactly-once guarantee. RLS ENABLED (defense-in-depth) per the multi-tenant rule; runtime isolation is AdminRepo + explicit tenant filter (the coordination.ex convention, coordination.ex:11-20).

`Coordination.claim(tenant_id, agent_id, project_id, ref, opts)` does an INSERT (never a read-then-insert): a successful insert returns {:ok, claim}; a UNIQUE violation on (tenant_id, project_id, ref) is caught via unique_constraint and returned as {:error, :already_claimed} -> the endpoint/MCP surfaces 409 already_claimed. project ownership is checked (Projects.get_project/2, coordination.ex:154 pattern); agent ownership checked (agent_owned/2, coordination.ex:292-297). The claim + an audit entry run in ONE AdminRepo.transaction (Multi), mirroring run_post/3 (coordination.ex:313-341).

`Coordination.done(tenant_id, agent_id, project_id, ref)` sets `done_at = now()` for the caller's OWN claim (claimant_agent_id must equal the caller — a non-owner gets {:error, :not_found}, byte-identical to a missing claim, no oracle). `Coordination.release(tenant_id, agent_id, project_id, ref)` deletes the caller's own OPEN claim so the ref can be re-claimed (an abandoned/mis-claimed handoff is freed). Both are audited in a Multi. A done or released claim frees/records the ref per its lifecycle.

A LIFECYCLE-AWARE sweep reclaims claims — it MUST NEVER delete an OPEN, unexpired claim. It removes only: (a) claims with `done_at` older than a retention window (e.g. done + 7d), and (b) claims whose `lease_expires_at < now()` AND `done_at IS NULL` (an abandoned lease — the ref reopens for re-claim). It does NOT apply the uniform 30-day channel_posts sweep (ChannelPostSweeper, channel_post_sweeper.ex) to claims: a blanket expiry would silently reopen the exactly-once window on a live-but-long-running claim. A separate worker (or a distinct predicate) enforces this.

MCP tools `channel_claim(project_id, ref, lease_seconds?)`, `channel_release(project_id, ref)`, `channel_done(project_id, ref)` are added (agent key) and shipped in the mcp-server publish. `channel_claim` surfaces the 409 already_claimed distinctly so a loser learns another agent owns it (and can move on) rather than double-acting.

Tenant isolation: a claim in tenant A is invisible/untouchable from tenant B — claim/release/done/read all filter tenant_id explicitly on the AdminRepo path; a cross-tenant ref returns {:error, :not_found} (no existence oracle). A tenant-isolation test case is included (per the multi-tenant rule).

CROSS-PROJECT gating (shares 40.D3's predicate): claim/release/done authorize the caller against the SPECIFIC project (membership / project-scoped key), NOT merely tenant ownership — using the SAME `project_writable_by_agent(tenant_id, agent_id, project_id)` predicate 40.D3 adds to the write path. Without this, a same-tenant agent that is not a member of a sibling project could CLAIM (and thereby block, via a never-completed lease) or RELEASE handoffs in that project — the exact cross-project blast radius 40.D3 closes for posting would stay open for claiming (E1 graduate already gates this way via its D3 dependency; claim must be symmetric). A non-member claim/release/done returns {:error, :not_found} — byte-identical to a missing claim, no oracle distinguishing 'not a member' from 'does not exist'. A test asserts a non-member cannot claim/release/done in a sibling project while its own project works. If 40.D3 has not yet landed, B1 ships its claim writes membership-gated on the same predicate (they are co-delivered — see the D3 dependency).

test_cases.name: first claim wins, second is 409 already_claimed
preconditions: tenant + project + two agents A,B; a ref "handoff:repo#812"

test_cases.name: concurrent claims — exactly one wins
preconditions: N agents racing the same ref
expected_results: exactly one {:ok}; the rest {:error, :already_claimed}; exactly one row in channel_claims

test_cases.name: done marks done_at; release frees for re-claim
steps: another agent claims after A release
expected_results: after release the ref can be claimed again by another agent

test_cases.name: non-owner cannot done/release someone else's claim
sweep never deletes an open unexpired claim
preconditions: an OPEN claim with lease_expires_at in the future; a DONE claim past its done-retention; an expired-lease OPEN claim
expected_results: open+unexpired survives; done+old removed; expired-lease-open removed (ref reopens)

test_cases.name: cross-tenant claim is invisible
preconditions: tenant B holds a claim on ref X in project P_B
expected_results: A cannot see or collide with B's claim; A's own claim on its own project is independent

technical_notes: WHY a dedicated table, not a keyed post (load-bearing): the shipped slot key is (tenant_id, project_id, agent_id, session_id, key) WHERE key IS NOT NULL (20260718000000:22-25), and insert_opts/1 (coordination.ex:355-365) makes EVERY keyed write an owner-scoped upsert. Two different agents claiming the same handoff would create two DISTINCT slots (different agent_id) — never a conflict, never a claim. Exactly-once REQUIRES the uniqueness to exclude the claimant, i.e. UNIQUE(tenant_id, project_id, ref). That cannot be expressed on channel_posts without breaking the working-state-slot semantics. Hence a new table.

CONCURRENCY ARGUMENT (state in the impl doc): INSERT ... with a UNIQUE(tenant_id, project_id, ref) constraint is atomic — Postgres serializes concurrent inserts on the unique index; exactly one commits, the rest raise a unique violation. Use Ecto unique_constraint/3 so the violation returns {:error, changeset} -> map to :already_claimed. This has NO TOCTOU window (unlike a SELECT-then-INSERT), which is precisely why the panel rejected the read-based 'claim via upsert'.

Follow the coordination.ex conventions exactly: AdminRepo (BYPASSRLS) + explicit tenant_id filter on every query (coordination.ex:11-20); claim/release/done each wrap the write + an Audit.log_in_multi entry in one AdminRepo.transaction (mirror run_post/3 coordination.ex:313-341 and run_delete/4 :227-267); UUID-guard the ref-lookup path (valid_uuid? pattern, coordination.ex:581-582 — though ref is a free string, guard project_id/tenant_id).

Sweep: a NEW Oban cron worker (Loopctl.Workers.ChannelClaimSweeper) modeled on ChannelPostSweeper (channel_post_sweeper.ex) but with the lifecycle-aware predicate in AC-40.B1.4 — NEVER `delete WHERE expires_at < now()` blanket. Batch-bounded + non-recursive like the existing sweeper (channel_post_sweeper.ex:51-78). Register in Loopctl.ObanConfig.plugins/0.

`ref` is a free string (e.g. "handoff:repo#812", or the 40.B2 stable handoff key) — the claim's identity is the ref, decoupled from any channel_posts row; a claim references a handoff post logically, not via FK, so a swept post does not orphan a live claim.

MCP: channel_claim / channel_release / channel_done in mcp-server/index.js (functions + tool defs alongside channel_post ~440-490, ~2266-2330). channel_claim must map 409 to a clear 'already claimed by another agent' message.

Sequencing: ships in step 5 (with 40.B2), after the read hardening (40.D1) and cursor (40.C2), before addressing (40.A5) feeds discovery (40.C1). NOTE: the CLAIM-write membership gate (AC-40.B1.7) shares 40.D3's `project_writable_by_agent` predicate, so 40.D3 (write scoping) must land with or before B1's claim writes — B1 now depends on 40.D3. If the original step-5-before-step-9 order is kept, pull D3's shared predicate forward (or co-deliver B1+D3); do NOT expose claim/release/done ungated.

AC-40.B1.7 (cross-project gating): reuse the EXACT predicate 40.D3 adds to post/3 (coordination.ex:154) — `project_writable_by_agent(tenant_id, agent_id, project_id)` — in claim/release/done, mapping non-membership to {:error, :not_found} so the endpoint returns the same oracle-safe 422/404 as a missing claim. Keep the predicate SHARED (a single helper) across post, claim, release, done, and graduate (40.E1) per 40.D3's technical note ('Also gate the CLAIM writes ... the same way ... keep the predicate shared').
